correctness.rationale: The projective-line multiset proof is correct. For a full-length \([2d+1,2,d]_q\) code, nonzero scalar classes correspond to points of \(\operatorname{PG}(1,q)\) and have weight \(2d+1-m(P)\). Minimum distance \(d\) forces a unique multiplicity \(d+1\); a full-weight word forces an empty point; the forbidden weights \(d+1,\ldots,d+t\) force every remaining multiplicity to be at most \(d-t\). The residual mass \(d\) must therefore fit on \(q-1\) points, giving \(d\le(q-1)(d-t)\). Conversely that capacity condition is sufficient by distributing the residual multiplicities. This proves the iff threshold.
